tasks.title: Count the stock
tasks.why: A blind count finds what really is on the shelf. A manager then approves it and the books follow the shelf.
before: No other count is open at this place.

steps.do: Open Stock Count (Menu → Operations → Stock Count). Check “Stock at” is your place.
Press “Start count”.
steps.see: Every item in use is listed.

steps.do: Count each item and type it in its box, in the unit shown. Type 0 for anything not there. Each box saves when you leave it (✓).
When every item has a number, press “Submit count”.
steps.see: “Count submitted for a manager to review.”

if.case: “Count every item before submitting — enter 0 for anything not there.”
if.do: Find the empty box and type its number.

if.case: “A count is already {status} here (started {when} by {who}). Finish or cancel it first”
if.do: Only one count at a time. Finish that count, or a manager cancels it.

if.case: The count was started by mistake
if.do: Press “Cancel this count…”, type why and press “Cancel the count”.

tasks.title: Review and approve a stock count
tasks.why: Approving posts the differences between the books and the shelf. Someone other than the counter must approve.
before: A count was submitted.

steps.do: Open Stock Count (or Approvals) and press “Review” on the submitted count.
Read Expected, Counted, Variance and Value for each item.
If it looks right, press “Approve and post variances”.
If something is wrong (a delivery not entered), type “Reason to reject (recount)” and press “Reject”. Fix the cause, then count again.

if.case: “A count must be approved by someone other than the person who counted it”
if.do: Another manager approves. You can “Withdraw for a recount”.

if.case: A big loss shows on one item
if.do: Check Purchasing for a delivery not entered and Inventory for losses not recorded before approving.

tasks.title: Open the day with Start of Day
tasks.why: One list for the morning: the drawer counted, people clocked in, what to make, deliveries due, nothing low without an order, red alerts answered.

steps.do: Open Start of Day (Menu → Operations → Start of Day; for the owner and general manager under More). From 04:00 the Dashboard also shows “Opening up? The start of the day, step by step”.
Step “Drawer open and counted”: press “Open the drawer”, count, and add a float from the safe if needed.
Step “Everyone due in is in”: late people clock in on the till (“Clock in on the till”).
Step “What to make today”: press “Open the plan” and tell the kitchen.
Step “Deliveries due”: press “Receive them” when they come. Step “Nothing low without an order”: press “What to buy”.
Step “Red alerts answered”: press “Answer them”.
When all are ticked:

if.case: The opening count differs from last night's close
if.do: Count again. If it still differs, open anyway: the difference is recorded.

if.case: A delivery is late
if.do: It stays in Deliveries due. Call the supplier and receive it when it comes.

tasks.title: Approve what is waiting for a manager
tasks.why: Counts, losses over the limit, purchase orders and the month's pay wait for a manager. Approvals shows them all, oldest first.

steps.do: Open Approvals (at the top of the menu; the number shows how many wait).
Read each card: what it is, who asked, when and why. Press “Open its page” to see more.
Press “Approve” if it is right.
If not: press “Send back for a recount…”, “Reverse…” (a loss) or “Cancel the order…”, type why, and press “Confirm”.
Losses can also be approved on Inventory under “Losses waiting for approval”: “Approve”, or “Reverse…” and “Reverse the loss: the stock goes back”.

if.case: No Approve button on a count or loss
if.do: You asked for it yourself. Another manager approves it.

if.case: An order shows “Over your limit”
if.do: The owner or general manager approves it.

if.case: The month's pay looks wrong
if.do: Open its page and reopen or draft it again there. There is no send-back for pay.

if.case: The accountant sees only the month's pay
if.do: That is right: the accountant approves pay only.

tasks.title: Void a sale rung by mistake
tasks.why: A void takes the whole sale back exactly: money, stock and points. It is possible only until the drawer session is closed.
before: The drawer session that holds the sale is still open.

steps.do: Open Orders (Menu → Operations → Orders) and press “Today”, or type the 8 letters after “Sale” on the receipt in “Find a sale” and press “Find”.
On the sale press “Void”.
Choose “Why void it?” (Rang twice, Rang the wrong item…) and add a note.
In “Approved by” choose a second manager and let them type their PIN, or “No second person (the owner reviews it)”.
Press “Confirm void”.
steps.see: “Voided (journal {no}).” The cash leaves the drawer's session.

if.case: The drawer was already closed
if.do: Use “Refund” instead.

if.case: A cashier asks for a void
if.do: Cashiers cannot open Orders. A manager does it.

if.case: The till discarded a payment that may have gone through
if.do: Look for the sale here. If it is there and was not paid, void it.

tasks.title: Refund part of a sale
tasks.why: When the customer brings something back after the drawer is closed, a refund gives the money back the way it was paid.
before: The sale is Completed or Part-refunded.

steps.do: Open Orders and find the sale (by its number, the customer's name or phone, or the day).
Press “Refund”.
In “Refund now” set how many of each item go back. Set the others to 0.
Choose “Why refund it?”. If it is over the refund limit, choose who approves and let them type their PIN.
Press “Confirm refund”.
Give the money back and press “Print the refund slip”.

if.case: “Over {limit}, a second person approves it: choose who, and they type their PIN.”
if.do: Ask another manager to approve.

if.case: The sale was paid in two ways
if.do: Type how much goes back on each way (at most what is left on each).

if.case: The tip
if.do: A tip is never given back.

tasks.title: Close the day with End of Day
tasks.why: One list for closing: bills paid, everyone clocked out, drawers counted, losses approved, card and platform money, red alerts. Then the day in numbers.

steps.do: Open End of Day (Menu → Operations → End of Day). From 16:00 the Dashboard shows “Closing up? The end of the day, step by step”.
Step “Bills paid”: take payment for open bills on the till (“Open the till”).
Step “Everyone clocked out”: “Open the hours” and fix anyone still in.
Step “Drawers closed and counted”: press “Close the drawer” on each, count, and close.
Step “Losses approved”: press “Approve them”. Step “Card and platform money”: check card takings.
Read “The day in numbers”. Press “Print or save as PDF”, or “Print the slip for the till”.

if.case: A cashier went home with the drawer open
if.do: Press “Close it for them”, write “Why it is closed”, and count if you can. Press “Close the session”, or “Close it without a count”.

if.case: The count is short
if.do: Count again. If still short, close: the difference shows on the slip and on Sales → Cash Sessions.

if.case: A table did not pay
if.do: Leave the bill open for the next session, or cancel it on the till with the reason if it will never be paid.

tasks.title: Move cash between the till, the safe and the bank
tasks.why: A float into the till, the day's cash to the bank: each move is recorded so the till, safe and bank stay right.

steps.do: Open Sales (Menu → Revenue → Sales) and go to “Move Cash”.
Choose From (the till, the safe, the bank, the owner) and To.
Type “Amount (IQD)” and a note (for example Deposit at the bank).
Press “Move cash”.

if.case: Money to or from the owner
if.do: Only the owner can take cash for the owner, and a reason is required.

if.case: The bank and an app (FIB)
if.do: Money from a way to pay moves on Sales → Ways to Pay, not here.

tasks.title: Set today's dollar rate and change dollars for dinars
tasks.why: The till takes dollars only with a fresh rate. Dollars taken go to the safe and are changed later.

steps.do: Open Sales → Dollars.
Owner, general manager or branch manager: type “Today's rate: dinars a dollar” and “Where it comes from” (for example the exchange office this morning). Press “Set the rate”.
To change dollars: under “Exchange dollars for dinars” choose From (the safe or a till), type the Dollars and the “Dinars received”, choose Into, and press “Exchange”.
steps.see: “{usd} exchanged for {received}: they were taken at {value}.”

if.case: The accountant cannot set the rate
if.do: Only the owner, general manager and branch manager set it. The accountant can record an exchange.

if.case: A cashier says dollars are not offered
if.do: The rate is too old. Set today's rate.

tasks.title: Send stock to another place, and receive it
tasks.why: The kitchen sends gelato to a branch: the stock leaves one place at its cost and arrives at the other. What does not arrive is written off.
before: The café has two or more places.

steps.do: At the sending place open Transfers (Menu → Operations → Transfers).
Choose From and To. Add each Item, Quantity and Unit; “+ Add line” for more. Add a note.
Press “Send it”.
At the other place, under “On their way”, press “Received: all of it”.
If some did not arrive: press “Not all of it arrived…”, type “What arrived of {item}” and a note, then “Receive what arrived”.

if.case: Sent to the wrong place
if.do: At the sending place, while it is on its way: “Cancel it…”, type why, “Cancel the transfer”. Then send again.

if.case: It warns stock goes below zero
if.do: Usually a batch or delivery is not recorded. Fix that, or press “Send it all the same” if you are sure.

tasks.title: Make next week's schedule
tasks.why: The schedule says who works when. Late, early and absent are worked out from it, and it is checked against how busy each hour usually is.
before: People are on Staff with “Where they work”.

steps.do: Open Staff → “The schedule” and press “The week after”.
Press “The same hours as the week before” to copy last week.
Change what differs: type hours like 08:00-16:00 in a person's box; empty means not working.
Read the check “Is the week staffed for how busy it usually is?” under the grid.
Press “Save the week”.
For a closer look, open Reports → “Staffed when busy? Orders an hour against who was on the clock →”.

if.case: A shift goes past midnight
if.do: Type 18:00-02:00. It ends the next morning.

if.case: You saved the wrong week
if.do: Press “Undo ({n})” within 10 seconds, or correct and save again.

if.case: A day cannot change
if.do: That month's pay is approved. Reopen the payroll first.

tasks.title: Correct someone's hours
tasks.why: Forgot to clock out, the till was down, the wrong person clocked in: correct the hours before the payroll.
before: The month's payroll is not approved yet.

steps.do: Open Staff → “The hours”.
Find the record (for example “Still in”). Press “Correct…”.
Type the right In and Out times and “Why”. Press “Save the correction”.
Nobody clocked? Press “+ Add hours nobody clocked…”, choose Who, In, Out and Why, and press “Add the hours”.
Wrong person? Press “Cancel…” on that record, type why, and press “Cancel this record”.

if.case: Late or absent: do they lose pay?
if.do: Not by itself. Deduct it on the payroll line with “Adjust…” if the café decides so.

tasks.title: When someone forgets their PIN, loses their phone or leaves
tasks.why: A new PIN or phone keeps them clocking in. A last day stops their clock-ins and schedule, but keeps their records and pay.

steps.do: Open Staff and press the person's line.
Forgot the PIN: open “New PIN”, let them type a PIN twice, press “Save the PIN”.
steps.see: “{name} clocks in with this PIN now.”

steps.do: Lost the phone: open “Their phone”, press “Unlink…”, type why, “Unlink the phone”. Later press “Link a new phone”.
Leaving: make sure they are clocked out. Open “Last day”, choose the date, type why, press “Save their last day”.
Owner or general manager: on Settings → People and roles press “Deactivate” on their row so their login stops.

if.case: They come back
if.do: Open their line → “Works here again”, type why, press “They work here again”. On Settings press “Reactivate”.

if.case: “Too many wrong PINs”
if.do: A new PIN also lifts the pause.

tasks.title: Correct stock outside a count
tasks.why: You found a box not in the books, or the books show stock that is not there and no count is due.

steps.do: Open Inventory and press “Correct stock (manager)”.
Choose the Item. Type the change in “Change (− to reduce)” (for example -250) and the Unit.
For an addition, type “Cost per base unit (additions)” if you know it.
Type “Why (required)” and press “Post correction”.
A large change asks again: press “Yes, post it”, or “Change it” to fix the numbers.

if.case: An item shows negative stock
if.do: Usually a delivery was not entered. Enter it on Purchasing instead of correcting.

if.case: A count is due soon
if.do: Count instead; the count corrects everything at once.

tasks.title: Answer or snooze an alert on the Dashboard
tasks.why: Red alerts need someone now; orange can wait. Answering says what was done, so the next person does not check again.

steps.do: Open the Dashboard and look at “Needs you”.
Press the alert's “{action} →” link to go where it is fixed. Fix it.
If it is fine, press “Answer”, write “What was done, or why it is fine”, and press “Save the answer”.
If it can wait, press “Snooze”, choose “Snooze until”, write “Why it can wait”, and press “Snooze it”.

if.case: The alert names you (your own exceptions)
if.do: You cannot answer it. Another manager or the owner reviews it.

if.case: An alert disappeared by itself
if.do: Its cause cleared (the drawer counted, the bill paid). Nothing to do.

if.case: Alerts come too often
if.do: The owner or general manager changes the limits on Settings → Alerts.

tasks.title: Change a customer's details or give them points
tasks.why: Fix a name or phone, add a delivery address, or give points that were missed.

steps.do: Open Customers (Menu → Revenue → Customers). Search by name or 3+ digits of the number.
Press the customer's name.
Press “Change their details”, change Name, Phone or Notes, and Save.
For an address press “+ Add an address” and “Add the address”.
For points: type “Points” (50, or -20 to take), “Why”, and press “Give or take them”.

if.case: The customer should no longer show at the till
if.do: Press “Put them away”. Their history stays; “Bring back” returns them.

if.case: A cashier cannot open Customers
if.do: Cashiers add customers at the till only.

tasks.title: Make this week's orders with What to buy
tasks.why: What to buy works out what is low and what is coming, and suggests packs, supplier and price. The ticked lines become draft orders.
before: Items have a usual supplier and a price, or past deliveries.

steps.do: Open Purchasing and press “Open What to buy”.
Each supplier has a card. Check the ticked lines: Quantity, Pack, “Price of a pack” and Supplier.
Press “How it was worked out” on a line to see why.
Untick what you do not want. For an extra item, open “Not to order now” and press “Add to an order”.
Press “Create the orders”.
steps.see: “{n} draft orders made, for a manager to approve:”

steps.do: Faster: on Purchasing press “Draft the orders now” to make every draft in one press.

if.case: Another supplier is cheaper
if.do: Press “Order from {supplier}, {pct} cheaper”. Tick “Make it the usual one” to keep using them.

if.case: The quantity is too much for the shelf
if.do: Lower it, or type “Days it keeps once it comes” under How it was worked out and press Save.

if.case: No price is known
if.do: Type the price of a pack. It is remembered next time.

tasks.title: Make a purchase order by hand
tasks.why: For an item not on What to buy, or a special order for an event.
before: The supplier and the items exist.

steps.do: Open Purchasing and press “New order”.
Choose the Supplier. Type the Expected day and a “Note for the supplier” if needed.
For each line choose the Item, type Quantity, choose the Unit and type “Price per unit”. Press “Add a line” for more.
Press “Save the draft”.
steps.see: “Order {no} saved as a draft: {total}. A manager approves it next.”

if.case: “Save the draft” stays grey
if.do: Every line needs an item, a quantity above zero and a price.

tasks.title: Approve, send, close or cancel a purchase order
tasks.why: An order is approved by a manager within their limit, then sent to the supplier. It is closed when the rest will not come.
before: A draft order exists.

steps.do: Open Purchasing → Purchase orders.
Manager: press “Approve”, or “Approve and send” to approve and mark it sent in one tap.
steps.see: “Order {no} approved and marked as sent to the supplier.”

steps.do: To give the supplier a paper copy, press the order number and “Print the order”.
Purchasing (or a manager) after sending an approved order: press “Mark as sent”.
If the rest will never come: press “Close”, type “Why is the rest not coming?”, press “Close the order”.
Wrong order and nothing came: press “Cancel”, type “Why cancel it?”, press “Cancel the order”.

if.case: “Over your limit: the owner or the general manager approves it”
if.do: It waits for them on Approvals.

if.case: A wrong price on an approved order not yet sent
if.do: Press “Change”, fix it and save. It is a draft again and is approved again.

if.case: Purchasing sees no Approve button
if.do: Purchasing cannot approve. A manager does.

tasks.title: Receive a delivery
tasks.why: Receiving brings the goods into stock at what they really cost, with freight shared over the lines. The bill is recorded later on Vendors.
before: The supplier exists. For an order: it is Approved or Sent.

steps.do: Open Purchasing → “Receive stock (goods receipt)”.
Choose the Supplier. If there is an order, choose it in “Against a purchase order”: the lines fill in.
Change each line's Quantity to what came. Check the Unit and type “Price per {unit} (IQD)” exactly as the invoice gives it.
Type “Freight (IQD)” or “Other landed costs” if on the invoice, and the delivery note number in Note.
Press “Receive goods”.
steps.see: “Receipt {no} — {value} into stock against order {po}, awaiting its bill.”

steps.do: If a warning card asks about a price, check it. Press “The price is right: receive it” or “Let me correct it”.
Press the paperclip on the delivery to keep a photo of the delivery note.

if.case: The item is not in Inventory yet
if.do: On the line choose “+ New item (not in Inventory yet)…”, fill it in and add it.

if.case: Only part of the order came
if.do: Receive what came. The order shows Partly received; receive the rest later or close it.

if.case: The invoice is in kilograms but the item is kept in grams
if.do: Choose the kg unit on the line and type the price per kg.

tasks.title: Correct or reverse a delivery entered wrong
tasks.why: A wrong quantity, price, item, supplier or date on a delivery can be fixed before its bill is recorded.
before: The delivery is not billed (cancel its bill on Vendors first) and its month is not locked.

steps.do: Open Purchasing → “Recent goods receipts”.
Press “Correct” on the delivery.
Change the Supplier, “The day it came”, or the lines (Item, Quantity, Unit, Price per unit).
Press “Show what it would do” and read the answer.
Type “Why it is corrected” and press “Confirm the correction”.
Entered twice? Press “Reverse”, type why, and press “Reverse the delivery”.

if.case: No Correct button
if.do: It is billed, reversed or old. Cancel the bill on Vendors first (only if nothing is paid on it).

if.case: It leaves stock below zero
if.do: Tick “This leaves {items} below zero: correct it all the same” if you are sure.

tasks.title: Send goods back to a supplier
tasks.why: Damaged, out of date or wrong goods go back. The stock goes out and the supplier owes the café for them.
before: The goods are in stock at this place.

steps.do: Open Purchasing → “Return goods to a supplier”.
Choose the Supplier and, if you can, “The delivery they came in”.
Choose the Item, Quantity and Unit for each line.
Type “Why they are going back” and press “Return them”.
steps.see: “Return {no}: {value} back to the supplier, off what the delivery's bill will clear.”

steps.do: Press the paperclip under “Recent returns to suppliers” to keep a photo of the return note.

if.case: The bill was already paid
if.do: Name the delivery. The return becomes a credit; set it against the next bill on Vendors → Credit notes.

if.case: It would leave stock below zero
if.do: Check the item. Press “Return it all the same” if you are sure.

tasks.title: Keep a photo of a delivery note, bill or receipt
tasks.why: The paper is kept with its record, so anyone checking later can see it.
before: The record exists (a delivery, a return, a bill, a credit note or an expense).

steps.do: Press the paperclip next to the record (“No documents kept with it yet”).
Press “Take a photo” (on a phone) or “Choose a picture or a PDF”.
Check the Name, add a Note if useful, and press “Attach”.

if.case: The wrong photo was attached
if.do: Press “Take off”, type why (“wrong photo”), press “Take it off”, and attach the right one.

if.case: The photo is huge
if.do: Attach it: pictures over 1.5 MB are made smaller first.

tasks.title: Record a supplier's bill
tasks.why: The bill turns a delivery into money owed to the supplier, with its due date. Services and rent are billed too.
before: For goods: the delivery was received on Purchasing.

steps.do: Open Vendors (Menu → Spending → Vendors), press the supplier, and open “Bills & payments”.
Choose “For goods received” and the delivery in “Goods receipt”. (For rent or repairs choose “For a service or asset” and “Charge to account”.)
Type the supplier's own number over “Invoice no.”, the “Invoice date” and the “Amount (IQD)” from the invoice.
Choose Terms (Due now, Net 7, 15 or 30 days).
Press “Record bill”.

if.case: The bill is more or less than the delivery
if.do: If the delivery was entered wrong, correct it on Purchasing first. If the supplier really charged it, record it: the difference goes to 5050 Purchase price variance.

if.case: A bill was entered twice
if.do: Owner, general manager or accountant: press “Cancel” on it, type why, choose the date, “Confirm”. Only while nothing is paid on it.

if.case: “(no unbilled receipts)”
if.do: This supplier has no delivery waiting for a bill. Receive the delivery first.

tasks.title: Pay a supplier's bill
tasks.why: Paying records where the money came from and lowers what is owed. Part payments are fine.
before: The bill is recorded. From the till: the drawer is open and holds enough. From the safe: it holds enough.

steps.do: Open Vendors, press the supplier and open “Bills & payments”.
Under “Pay bill” choose the bill. The amount fills with what is outstanding.
Change “Amount (IQD)” for a part payment.
Choose “Paid from” (The till, The safe, The bank, A card, The owner, personally).
Press “Record payment”.
steps.see: “Payment recorded (journal {no}). {amount} still outstanding on that bill.”

if.case: The owner paid from his own pocket
if.do: Choose “The owner, personally”. It is booked as money the owner put in.

if.case: A branch manager or purchasing cannot pay
if.do: Only the owner, general manager and accountant pay bills.

if.case: Which bills first?
if.do: Look at the ageing at the top of Vendors and pay the oldest first.

tasks.title: Record a supplier's credit note and use it
tasks.why: A credit is money the supplier owes back: goods returned after the bill, a lower price agreed, or an overcharge.

steps.do: Open Vendors, press the supplier, and open “Credit notes”.
For a return already listed (“Awaiting their note”): type the number on their credit note and press “Record it”.
For a new credit: under “Record their credit note” choose “A lower price on a delivery that was billed” or “Other: a service, an overcharge”.
Type “The number on their credit note”, “Amount (IQD)”, choose the delivery or the bill and account, and type “What it is for”. Press “Record the credit”.
Owner, general manager or accountant: on a credit with something left choose a bill in “Set it against”, check the Amount, press “Set against it”.
steps.see: “Set against the bill: {left} of the credit left.”

if.case: The supplier's number was used already
if.do: Each credit note number is accepted once per supplier.

tasks.title: Record an expense (rent, electricity, a small purchase)
tasks.why: Money spent that is not stock goes to an expense account, from the till, safe, bank, card or the owner.
before: The month is open. From the till: the drawer is open and holds enough.

steps.do: Open Expenses (Menu → Spending → Expenses).
Type “Narration” (for example September shop rent). An account is proposed from the words.
Type “Amount (IQD)” and the Date. From the till or safe the date must be today.
Choose “Paid from” and check the “Account”.
Press “Post expense”.
Press the paperclip on the new line to keep the receipt's photo.

if.case: It warns a payment like this was posted in the last 3 days
if.do: If it is the same payment, do not post. If it is a second payment, tick “It is another payment, not the same one” and post.

if.case: The words say waste, expired or damaged
if.do: That is a stock loss: record it on Inventory → Record a loss.

if.case: Wrong account or amount after posting
if.do: It cannot be edited. The accountant reverses its journal on Journals, then you post it again.

tasks.title: Record a payment made ahead for months (rent, insurance)
tasks.why: Three months' rent paid today belongs to three months. Each month takes its share.

steps.do: Open Expenses. Type the Narration, Amount, “Paid from” and Account.
Tick “Paid ahead for months to come (next month's rent, a year's insurance): each month takes its share”.
Choose “First month” and type “How many months”.
Press “Post prepaid expense”.
Each new month: under Prepaid Expenses press “Release what is due ({n})”.
steps.see: “{n} month(s)' share posted as an expense of its month.”

if.case: It was entered with the wrong months
if.do: Owner, general manager or accountant: press “Cancel”, type why, “Confirm”. Then record it again.

if.case: The Dashboard says a prepaid share is due
if.do: Press “Release what is due”.

tasks.title: Check the bank against its statement
tasks.why: Ticking each bank line the statement shows proves the books' bank agrees with the real bank, and finds what is missing.
before: The bank's statement as a file (.xlsx, .csv) or copied from the bank's site.

steps.do: Open Chart of Accounts → “The bank against its statement →”.
Press “Read it from its file…” and choose the file (or “or paste it”).
For a line not in the books: press “Record it” (a bank charge opens Expenses; interest opens a journal). Card money goes on Sales → Card Takings; platform money on Delivery Platforms.
Type “The statement's last day” and “The balance on the statement”.
Tick each line in “On the statement”, or press “Tick every line to this day”.
When it ties, press “Keep the statement”.
steps.see: “Statement {no} is kept: the bank ties to {date}.”

if.case: A transfer is in the books but not yet on the statement
if.do: Leave it unticked. It waits for the next statement.

if.case: A statement was kept by mistake
if.do: Press “Undo…” on the latest, type why, “Undo the statement”.

if.case: The file is .xls or PDF
if.do: Save it as .xlsx or .csv from Excel first.

tasks.title: Record card and app money reaching the bank
tasks.why: Card and app money waits in its own account until it reaches the bank. Settling moves it and records the fee.
before: The terminal's report, and the bank's statement or app's report.

steps.do: Open Sales → “Card Takings”.
Choose “Settle the days up to”. Type “The terminal's total (IQD)” or press “Same as the till”.
Type “Reached the bank (IQD)”, “Arrived on” and the “Bank reference (optional)”.
If the till and the terminal differ, write why in the Note. Press “Record the settlement”.
steps.see: “Settled (journal {no}): {fee} card fee; the till and the terminal agree.”

steps.do: For FIB, FastPay and others: in “Ways to Pay” choose From (the app) and To (the bank), type “What arrived (IQD)”, “Fee kept (IQD)” and the Day. Press “Move money”.

if.case: A settlement was wrong
if.do: Press “Cancel…” on the latest settlement, type why, and press “Cancel it”. Its days wait again.

if.case: A branch manager cannot settle
if.do: Only the owner, general manager and accountant settle card takings.

tasks.title: Match a delivery platform's payout
tasks.why: The platform pays for many orders at once, less its commission. Matching its statement to the orders checks every order was paid.
before: The platform's statement (Excel or CSV) and the payout in the bank.

steps.do: Open Delivery Platforms → “Match a Statement”. Choose the Platform.
Press “Read it from its file…” (or paste the rows in “The statement”).
Press “Match to the orders waiting” and read: orders matched, paid, not explained.
Type “Statement number or date” and “The payout arrived on”. If some lines do not match, say why in the Note.
Press “Post the payout”.

if.case: An order on the statement is not found
if.do: Check its number on Orders. If it was rung with a wrong number, write it in the note and post the rest.

if.case: A branch manager sees “The owner or the accountant posts the payout.”
if.do: They can match, but only the owner, general manager or accountant posts.

tasks.title: Post or reverse a journal by hand
tasks.why: For entries no screen makes (an accrual, interest), or to undo a wrong manual journal or expense with a mirror entry.
before: The month of the date is open.

steps.do: Open Journals (Menu → Accountant → Journals) and press “New Journal”.
Type “Date *” and “Notes *” (what it is for).
On each line choose the Account and type Debits or Credits. Press “+ Add line” for more.
Press “Save and publish” when debits equal credits (or “Save as draft”, then “Publish” later).
To undo a journal: press its number in the register, press “Reverse”, choose “Date of the reversal”, type “Why is it being reversed?”, press “Post reversal”.

if.case: A sale's or bill's journal is wrong
if.do: It has no Reverse button. Void or refund the sale on Orders, or cancel the bill on Vendors.

if.case: “Debits and credits must agree”
if.do: Fix the amounts until both sides are equal.

if.case: An account is missing from the list
if.do: Accounts with their own records (till, stock, payables…) are posted only by their screens.

tasks.title: Run the month's payroll and pay salaries
tasks.why: The payroll is drafted from each person's pay and hours, adjusted with reasons, approved, and then paid.
before: Everyone's pay is set on Staff.
Hours are corrected and everyone is clocked out.
To approve: the month is over.

steps.do: Open Payroll (Menu → Spending → Payroll). Choose “The month” and press “Draft the payroll”.
Read each line. Press “Adjust…” to add a bonus or a deduction with what it is for, or the advance to take back. Save.
If hours or pay changed since, press “Draft it again”.
Press “Approve the payroll”.
Choose “Paid from” and press “Pay everyone still owed ({amount})”, or “Pay…” on one line.
Press “Print or save as PDF” for the paper copy.

if.case: Approved with a mistake
if.do: If nothing is paid: “Reopen…” with why, fix, “Draft it again”, approve. If paid: cancel the payments first under Salaries paid.

if.case: “Approve the payroll” stays grey
if.do: The month is not over yet, or the draft is out of date: press “Draft it again”.

if.case: Paid the wrong person
if.do: Under Salaries paid press “Cancel…” with why, then pay the right line.

tasks.title: Give an advance on pay
tasks.why: Money given before payday. The next payroll takes it back by itself.
before: From the till: a drawer is open here and holds enough.

steps.do: Open Payroll and press “+ Give an advance…”.
Choose To, type the Amount, choose “Paid from” (The safe to start), and type what it is for.
Press “Give the advance”.

if.case: It was entered twice
if.do: Press “Cancel…” on the extra one with why. Only before a payroll took any of it back.

if.case: The drawer does not hold enough
if.do: Choose The safe or The bank.

tasks.title: Close the month
tasks.why: Locking a month stops any more posting into it, so its figures stay as reported.
before: Every trading day's cash counted, no stock count waiting, no draft journals, earlier months locked, payroll approved.

steps.do: Open Chart of Accounts (Menu → Accountant → Chart of Accounts) and press the month.
Read the checklist under “Close {period}”. Fix each failing check: its line says what is wrong.
Type a “Note for the audit trail (optional)”.
Press “Lock {period}”.
steps.see: “{period} is locked. Corrections now go in by reversing entries in an open period.”

if.case: “Every trading day's cash is counted” fails with “Not counted: {day}”
if.do: Close and count that day's drawer on End of Day, then reload.

if.case: “Resolve the {n} failing check(s) first.”
if.do: The button stays grey until every blocking check passes.

if.case: A mistake is found in a locked month
if.do: Correct it in the open month (reverse with today's date). Only the owner reopens, with a reason: “Why must it be reopened? (required)” and “Reopen {period}” (the latest locked month only).

tasks.title: Add equipment, or a new account, to the books
tasks.why: An oven or gelato machine loses value each month. The books show what it cost and what it is worth now. New kinds of cost, a second bank or a loan need their own account.
before: To pay it with a loan, add the loan account first.

steps.do: Open Chart of Accounts and scroll to Equipment. Press “＋ Add equipment”.
Type “What is it?”, “What it cost”, “Months it will be used”, “Worth at the end (0 if nothing)” and “Bought on”.
Choose “How was it paid?” and press “Add it”.
Each month press “Post it” to post the depreciation for months gone.
Sold or thrown out: press “Sold or thrown out”, type When and “What it fetched”, and Save.

if.case: It was bought years ago and is in the opening balances
if.do: Choose “Bought before: in the books already”: no money moves.

if.case: You need a new account (a kind of cost, a second bank, a loan)
if.do: In the accounts list choose “Type (Add an account)” (A cost, An income, Another bank account, A loan, A kind of equipment). The Code fills itself. Type “Name (English)” and press “Add the account”.

if.case: An account is no longer used
if.do: Press “Take out of use…” on it, type why and confirm. Its history stays in reports.

tasks.title: Record the owner putting money in or taking it out
tasks.why: Money between the owner and the bank or safe is not income or expense. It is the owner's money.

steps.do: Open Chart of Accounts and scroll to “The owner's money”.
Choose “The owner puts money in” or “The owner takes money out”, and The bank or The safe.
Type the Amount and “What it is for (required)”. Press “Record it”.

if.case: “Only the owner takes money out for themselves”
if.do: Only the owner records taking money out.

if.case: The owner paid a bill from his pocket
if.do: Record it on Expenses with “Paid from: The owner, personally”, not here.

tasks.title: Sell on account to a business and receive their payment
tasks.why: A hotel or office takes goods now and pays later. Each invoice is kept on their account until paid.
before: The business is a customer (Customers → “+ Add a customer”).

steps.do: Open Customers and press the customer's name. Press “Credit settings”.
Tick “Buys on account (pays later)”, type “Credit limit”, “Days to pay” and any wholesale % off. Save.
Press “＋ New invoice”. Add each Product and Quantity, and press “Make the invoice”.
When they pay: press “Receive a payment”, type the Amount, choose “Where did the money go?”, press “Receive it”.
Press “Statement” to print their account.

if.case: The invoice is over their limit
if.do: Raise the limit in Credit settings, or take a payment first.

tasks.title: Read today's figures on the Dashboard
tasks.why: Today against a usual day and the target, what needs someone, and what the figures say in words.

steps.do: Open the Dashboard (first in the menu).
Read the four figures: “Net sales today”, “Orders”, “Average order value”, “Gross profit after waste & fees”. Tap one to see what is behind it.
Read “Needs you” and deal with the red alerts first.
Read “What the figures say” and “Yesterday” (the daily brief). Each sentence links to where to act.
Check the badge “Books reconcile” at the top. If it says “{n} reconciliation difference(s)”, open it.

if.case: No target card
if.do: Set the daily sales target on Settings → Rules (owner or general manager).

if.case: On a phone the charts are hidden
if.do: Press “Show the rest: charts, stock, recent sales”.

tasks.title: Read the month's reports and print them
tasks.why: The profit and loss, sales, buying, losses, staff and the balance sheet, for any dates and any place.

steps.do: Open Reports (Menu → Accountant → Reports). Press “Last month” (or type From and To and press “Show”).
With more than one place, choose the Place.
Read “The period at a glance” and “What the period says”.
Jump to Profit & Loss. Press an account line to see its journal lines.
Press “The month at a glance →” for the month against the one before.
Press “Balance sheet and cash flow →” for what the café owns and owes.
Open the parts you want, then press “Print or save as PDF”.

if.case: “This screen could not be loaded” after changing dates
if.do: From must be on or before To. Fix the dates.

if.case: An expense is missing
if.do: It may be a draft journal (not counted) or have another date.

tasks.title: Check that the books tie
tasks.why: Each record (drawers, stock, suppliers, cards, platforms) must agree with its account. A difference means something to fix.

steps.do: Open Reports → Checks → “Do the books tie?”.
Open the table. Each row shows the Subledger, the Ledger and the difference.
For a difference, press “{n} record(s)” to see the records to look into, and press each one to open where it is kept.
Fix the cause there (an uncounted drawer, a missing journal), then look again.

if.case: The drawer check does not tie
if.do: Usually a session is not closed or counted. Open “Drawer sessions”.

if.case: Inventory (1200) does not tie and old app records are listed
if.do: Owner only: check them, type why, press “Post these {n} journal(s)”.

tasks.title: Look at voids, refunds and discounts
tasks.why: Exceptions show every void, refund, discount, cancelled bill and giveaway with who did it and why.

steps.do: Open Reports, choose the dates, and jump to Checks → Exceptions.
Read each row: who, when, the reason, and if a second person approved.
Rows without a second person need review. Talk to the person if a pattern shows.
Press “CSV” to keep the list.

if.case: A cashier has many voids
if.do: Read each reason and time. From now on ask a second person to approve voids.

tasks.title: Decide what to keep, reprice or drop on the menu
tasks.why: The menu matrix shows what sells and what earns. Price watch shows what came in dearer and the price that keeps the margin.
before: Products have recipes with costs.

steps.do: Open Reports → “Menu matrix: what to keep, reprice, show more or drop →”.
Choose “The last 4 weeks” or “The last 3 months”, and a category to compare like with like.
Read the four groups: Keep, Raise the price, Show it more, Change it or drop it.
Open Reports → “Price watch: what came in dearer →”.
Owner or general manager: press “Set it” beside a price to sell it at that price from today.

if.case: A new product shows “Change it or drop it”
if.do: It may just be new. Look again over The last 3 months.

if.case: The rise was a one-off
if.do: Do not change the price. The next delivery will show.

tasks.title: Check the cash will last the next 30 days
tasks.why: Cash ahead shows the bank and the safe day by day, with bills due and usual takings, and warns before money runs short.
before: Four weeks of takings, and supplier bills with due dates.

steps.do: Open Reports → “Cash ahead: the next 30 days of the bank and the safe →”.
Read the warnings at the top. Each says when and what to do.
Look at “Day by day” and “What is due and expected”.
Act: move cash, delay a bill, or chase customers who owe (“Customers”).

if.case: The Dashboard says money is short ahead
if.do: Open Cash ahead, read the warning, do its action, look again.

tasks.title: Look at the watch list
tasks.why: Patterns that stand out: voids far more than others, discounts just under the limit, a drawer short again and again.
before: Four weeks of sales. The general manager reads it only if the owner allows it.

steps.do: Open Reports → “Watch list: patterns worth a look →” (or the Dashboard's watch list card).
Read each finding. Press “The sales of those days” to see the sales.
Write “A note (on the audit trail)” and press “Explained” or “Looked into”.
Owner: to let the general manager help, tick “The general manager reads the watch list too” on Settings.

if.case: A finding has a good reason (an agreed discount)
if.do: Write it and press “Explained”.

tasks.title: Find who changed something
tasks.why: The audit trail keeps every change with the value before and after, who did it and why. Nobody can change it.

steps.do: Open Audit trail (Menu → Accountant → Audit trail).
Choose From and To, “What” (for example Prices) and “Who”. Press “Show”.
Read the rows. Press “CSV” to download the whole list.

if.case: A change shows “No one signed in”
if.do: It was made in the database directly. Ask whoever looks after the system.

if.case: Why was a month reopened?
if.do: Choose What → Books & periods; the Why column has the owner's reason.

tasks.title: Deal with problems staff reported
tasks.why: Staff report problems from “Something's wrong?”. Mark each one dealt with so nobody checks it twice.

steps.do: Open Menu → You → Reported problems (or the Dashboard card “{n} problem(s) reported by staff”).
Read the report: the screen, who, when and what went wrong.
Type “What was done (optional)” and press “Dealt with”.
If it needs whoever looks after the system, press “Copy to send on” and paste it into a message.

if.case: It happens again
if.do: Press “Open again” on the report.

tasks.title: Check stock use, waste and stock value
tasks.why: Usage compares what the counts say was used with what the recipes say. Waste by recipe shows what is thrown away. Stock value shows what stock was worth.
before: Two approved counts of each item in the dates (for Usage).

steps.do: Open Usage (Menu → Operations → Usage). Press “Last month” or choose dates.
Read the difference for each item. Press “What it is made of” to see why.
Open Reports → “Waste by recipe: made, sold and thrown away →”.
Open Reports → “Stock value on a day →”. Choose the day in On and press “Show”.

if.case: Milk shows a big difference
if.do: Check losses not recorded and portion sizes. Count again next week.

if.case: Stock value differs from 1200 Inventory
if.do: Check Do the books tie? on Reports.

tasks.title: Check a drawer session's cash
tasks.why: Each session shows what it opened with, every cash movement, what it should have held, what was counted and the difference.

steps.do: Open Sales → Cash Sessions → “All sessions”.
Choose From and To and press “Show”.
Press a Session to open its statement.
Read every cash movement: sales, refunds, voids, paid out, taken to the safe or bank. Press “Print” for paper.

if.case: A session is short
if.do: Look at its voids, refunds and paid-outs. Compare with the exceptions on Reports.

tasks.title: Download the books for checking
tasks.why: Every journal line, the trial balance and the audit trail can be downloaded for Excel.

steps.do: Open Reports, choose the dates, and press “every journal line (CSV)”.
Open Chart of Accounts, choose the month, and press “Download CSV” for the trial balance.
Press an account name to see its lines; press “CSV” there.
Open Journals to read each entry: press its number to see its lines.
Open Audit trail and press “CSV”.

if.case: The journal lines CSV is the whole café
if.do: It always is, whatever place is chosen.

tasks.title: Check a supplier's statement and the papers behind it
tasks.why: The statement shows each bill, payment and credit with the balance. The papers show the invoice behind each line.

steps.do: Open Vendors and press the supplier. On the Statement tab press “A statement between two dates, to print”.
Choose From and To and press “Show”.
Press a paperclip to see the invoice or credit note kept with that line.
Press “Print the statement” for paper.

if.case: The supplier says the café owes a different amount
if.do: Print the statement for their dates and go through it line by line. Record any missing bill or credit on Vendors.
